papers.title_in_file: A quantum graph approach to metamaterial design
papers.version_note: Published form (Scientific Reports 2022, 12:18006); matches the record title.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, model sections, results and conclusion.
papers.what_it_is: A classical wave-physics paper that models 2D metamaterials as periodic quantum graphs with unitary vertex scattering matrices.
papers.why_not: The paper uses quantum graphs as a mathematical model of classical wave transport in metamaterials. It has no qubits, quantum circuits, quantum hardware or machine learning workload, so it bears on none of the contexts.

papers.title_in_file: Accelerated quantum Monte Carlo with mitigated error on noisy quantum computer
papers.version_note: File is arXiv:2106.09880v3 (5 Jan 2022); matches the record title.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, conclusions; method derivations and appendices skimmed only.
papers.what_it_is: A theory paper proposing quantum-circuit Monte Carlo, a hybrid non-variational algorithm that uses quantum time-evolution circuits to ease the sign problem in quantum Monte Carlo.

assertions.value: The authors state that the quantum subroutine can be implemented with shallow circuits and, with error mitigation, can reduce the Monte Carlo variance by several orders of magnitude even when the circuit noise is significant.
quotes: The quantum subroutine can be implemented with shallow circuits and, by incorporating error mitigation, can reduce the Monte Carlo variance by several orders of magnitude even when the circuit noise is significant.
assertions.certainty_reason: Theoretical analysis and simulation by the authors; no hardware run is reported in the text read.

assertions.value: The authors state that they introduce a non-variational algorithm that uses quantum simulation as a subroutine to accelerate quantum Monte Carlo by easing the sign problem.
quotes: we introduce a novel non-variational algorithm using quantum simulation as a subroutine to accelerate quantum Monte Carlo by easing the sign problem.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its method.

assertions.value: The authors state that the complexity is polynomial on a fault-tolerant quantum computer but exponential on a noisy quantum computer because of the finite error rate.
